pride_data.title: The sodium leak channel NALCN is regulated by the neuronal SNARE complex
pride_data.projectDescription: Chemical cross-linking coupled to mass spectrometry was used to study the subunit organization of the complex between human NALCN, FAM155A, SNAP25 and STX1A proteins. Cross-linking data was generated using the reagents disuccinimidyl suberate (DSS), pimelic dihydrazide (PDH), and 4-(4,6-dimethoxy-1,3,5-triazin-2-yl)-4-methylmorpholinium (DMTMM) chloride.
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Cross-linking was performed according to previously described procedures (Leitner et al., Nat. Protoc., 2014; Mohammadi et al., Anal. Chem., 2021). Cross-linked proteins were digested in solution using endoproteinase Lys-C and trypsin and fractionated by size-exclusion chromatography. LC-MS/MS analysis was performed on a Thermo Orbitrap Fusion Lumos mass spectrometer.  Further information can be found in the accompanying publication.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: MS/MS spectra were searched using xQuest/xProphet (Walzthoeni et al., Nat. Methods, 2012), version 2.1.5, against the sequences of the target proteins and identified contaminants/copurified proteins (including calmodulin, which interacts specifically with the core complex). The false discovery rate was controlled by searching against reversed sequences. Important xQuest search settings were as follows: Enzyme = trypsin, maximum number of missed cleavages = 2, MS mass tolerance = 15 ppm, MS/MS mass tolerance = 15 ppm. Reactive sites for the cross-linking reagents were defined as follows: K and protein N terminus for DSS, D and E for PDH, K with D and K with E for DMTMM. The false discovery rate is <1% at the level of non-redundant cross-link peptide pairs. PDH cross-linking resulted in a very small number of identifications that are not included in this data set. The table “File_list.xlsx” allows the assignment of different cross-linking conditions, SEC fractions and replicates to the corresponding .raw files. Further information can be found in the accompanying publication.
keywords: Chemical cross-linking; dss; pdh; dmtmm; ion channel; sodium leak channel; nalcn; snare complex
